issues.title: No middleware.ts — authentication bypass possible
issues.description: The original console has middleware.ts that enforces cookie-based auth and SSO redirect for all authenticated routes. The migration has NO middleware.ts at the root level — only a stale copy in legacy/. Auth is enforced purely client-side via useAuth hook, which creates a window where server-rendered HTML is served to unauthenticated users before the client-side check runs.
issues.recommendation: Create middleware.ts at repo root. Copy auth logic from legacy/middleware.ts. Add Next.js matcher config to protect all routes except /onboarding and public pages.

issues.title: Main branch build fails — no force-dynamic on data-fetching pages
issues.description: Next.js App Router attempts static generation of all pages at build time. Pages that use Jotai atoms, useEffect, or axios calls fail with ECONNREFUSED because there is no backend available during build. The main branch has 0 pages with force-dynamic. feat/design-inspect fixes 63 pages by adding 'export const dynamic = force-dynamic' at the top of each page.tsx.
issues.recommendation: Merge feat/design-inspect into main. Add force-dynamic to the remaining 17 pages that still lack it. Long-term: migrate data fetching to React Suspense + Server Component boundaries to reduce pages needing force-dynamic.

issues.title: Agora-branded CSS component classes in globals.css violate utility-first rule
issues.description: src/styles/globals.css defines .agora-card, .agora-button-primary, .agora-button-secondary, .agora-sidebar, .agora-table, .agora-input, .agora-status-* and others as semantic CSS classes. These classes are used across 80 app pages. This violates the TailwindCSS utility-first rule in RULE.md which disallows custom CSS component classes. Design tokens as CSS variables are fine; component classes are not.
issues.recommendation: Phase 1: Keep for now to unblock shipping. Phase 2: Replace each usage with equivalent Tailwind utilities or extend shadcn components via cn() wrapper pattern. Remove the component class definitions from globals.css.

issues.title: typescript.ignoreBuildErrors = true in next.config.ts
issues.description: next.config.ts has typescript: { ignoreBuildErrors: true } carried forward from the original. This flag was a tech debt item in the original and has been blindly copied. It silently hides TypeScript errors during CI/CD. The 15 files with 'any' type usage (ISS-007) would be caught if this flag were removed.
issues.recommendation: Remove ignoreBuildErrors: true. Fix the resulting TypeScript errors. This is a one-time effort that pays compounding dividends.

issues.title: Form library not migrated — 11 Formik + 11 Yup files still present
issues.description: RULE.md mandates react-hook-form + zod for all forms. The original used Formik + Yup. The migration shows 11 Formik files and 11 Yup files — the same count as the original. Zero form migration progress. Affected pages include /settings/profile (OTP, phone, email, password), /settings/sso-management, /settings/teams-members, and several project management forms.
issues.recommendation: Audit each Formik form. Replace with react-hook-form + zodResolver + ShadCN Form components. Extract zod schemas to separate *-schema.ts files. Priority: /settings/profile (highest complexity, highest user risk).

issues.title: 340 'use client' directives — excessive client-side rendering
issues.description: The migration has 340 'use client' files. This essentially replicates the Pages Router client-side rendering model inside App Router, eliminating App Router's primary advantage (Server Components). Many components could be Server Components if data fetching were moved to server-side patterns. This inflates client bundle size and prevents streaming.
issues.recommendation: Audit 'use client' usage. Push the directive to leaf components only. Move data fetching to Server Components using the apiGet service layer already present on feat/design-inspect. Eliminate Jotai atoms that only hold server-fetched data (replace with props from Server Components).

issues.title: 15 files with 'any' type — violates TypeScript strict mode rule
issues.description: 15 files in the app directory use ': any', 'as any', or '<any>' type annotations. RULE.md mandates no 'any' type ever. Specific patterns found: payment response handlers, API response types, and third-party SDK type gaps.
issues.recommendation: Run 'grep -rn ": any\|as any" app/ src/' and fix each occurrence. Use unknown + type narrowing, or create explicit types for third-party responses. Remove typescript.ignoreBuildErrors so these are caught at build time.

issues.title: Inline style attributes on 2 components
issues.description: RULE.md disallows style={{...}} inline styles. Found on BillingDashboard chart container and one other component. These should be Tailwind utilities.
issues.recommendation: Replace inline styles with Tailwind equivalents. If the exact value isn't available as a Tailwind utility, use arbitrary value syntax: className='h-[340px]'.

issues.title: Typo in store filename: subsciptions.ts (missing 'r')
issues.description: Store file is named subsciptions.ts instead of subscriptions.ts. Imports referencing this file will be inconsistent and any future developer will need to remember the typo.
issues.recommendation: Rename to subscriptions.ts. Update all import references. Simple find-and-replace.

issues.title: reactStrictMode: false in next.config.ts
issues.description: React Strict Mode is disabled. This suppresses double-rendering in development that catches accidental side effects and deprecated API usage. Combined with ignoreBuildErrors, this reduces the development feedback loop quality.
issues.recommendation: Enable reactStrictMode: true. Fix any double-render issues that emerge (they indicate real bugs). This is especially important given the complexity of the data fetching patterns.

issues.title: Only 1 layout.tsx and 0 loading.tsx files — missing nested layouts and loading states
issues.description: The App Router has only 1 layout.tsx (root). There are no nested layouts for billing, project-management, settings, license-management, or subscriptions sections. There are no loading.tsx files for any section. The original had section-specific layouts (ProjectManagementLayout, SettingsSidebar, SignallingLayout) implemented via component composition — these are preserved as components but not as App Router layouts. Without loading.tsx, there are no streaming skeleton states.
issues.recommendation: Phase 1: Not blocking (the component-level layouts work). Phase 2: Convert to true App Router nested layouts for route grouping benefits. Add loading.tsx for complex sections (project-management, billing, settings) to enable streaming and improve perceived performance.

issues.title: Duplicate service files in feat/design-inspect — cleanup needed
issues.description: feat/design-inspect has service files in two locations: src/services/ (correct) and a root-level services/ directory (stale duplicate). The root-level services/ directory should be deleted.
issues.recommendation: Delete the root-level services/ directory. Verify all imports use src/services/. Do this before merging feat/design-inspect into main.

issues.title: Historical branches not cleaned up — 8 stale branches
issues.description: 8 branches exist that are no longer needed: migrate/pages (same SHA as main), migrate/pages-* (5 experiment branches all behind main), feat/dashboard (same SHA as main). These create confusion about which branch is canonical.
issues.recommendation: Delete: migrate/pages, migrate/pages-feature-components, migrate/pages-store, migrate/pages-hooks, migrate/pages-utils, migrate/pages-types, feat/dashboard. Evaluate playground branch for useful commits before deciding.

issues.title: 134 TODO comments in migration codebase
issues.description: 134 TODO/FIXME/HACK/TEMP comments spread across the migration codebase. RULE.md prohibits this. These represent unresolved technical decisions or incomplete implementations that could be silently shipped.
issues.recommendation: Audit all TODOs. Convert each to either: (a) a tracked issue, (b) a concrete code change, or (c) deletion if no longer relevant. Never ship with TODO comments.

issues.title: Incorrect payment status check in invoice components — logic bug
issues.description: In latest-invoice-table.tsx line 214: {'paymentStatus' in bill && !bill.paymentStatus} checks for falsy (0, null, undefined), but the invoices.tsx uses explicit === 1 (Paid), === 2 (Partial Paid) status codes. The latest-invoice-table uses !bill.paymentStatus which would show 'Unpaid' for any non-1 value including null/undefined, and 'Paid' for any truthy value. This diverges from the invoices.tsx logic and may cause incorrect status display for partial payments.
issues.recommendation: Align latest-invoice-table.tsx payment status logic with invoices.tsx: check paymentStatus === 1 for Paid, paymentStatus === 2 for Partial Paid, and fall through to Unpaid. Add 'Partial Paid' badge to latest-invoice-table.

issues.title: LicensePermissionGuard not implemented — license management pages unprotected
issues.description: The original console wraps /license-management/purchase-history, /license-management/pre-authorization, /license-management/quota-management, and /license-management/usages-query in LicensePermissionGuard which calls useLicensePermission() to gate access based on whether the user's account has license capabilities. Neither LicensePermissionGuard nor useLicensePermission exists in the migration. These pages are accessible to any authenticated user regardless of license status.
issues.recommendation: 1. Implement useLicensePermission hook: port logic from original console hooks directory. 2. Implement LicensePermissionGuard component wrapping shadcn card with access denied state. 3. Apply guard to all 4 license-management pages. 4. Consider implementing as a route group layout.tsx for App Router-native gating.

issues.title: Pre-authorization page is a placeholder — 3 components not migrated
issues.description:
The pre-authorization page renders only:

Pre Authorization

Pre-authorization functionality coming soon.

. The original has three complex tab components: ImportLicensesTab (~390 lines: file upload, license key input, validation, API submission), VerifyLicenseTab (~420 lines: license verification flow with status polling), ImportHistoryTab (import history table with pagination). None of these have been migrated.
issues.recommendation: Migrate all three components: 1. ImportLicensesTab — port from original, replace Formik with react-hook-form+zod, replace custom file upload with shadcn-compatible pattern. 2. VerifyLicenseTab — port polling logic, replace Formik. 3. ImportHistoryTab — port table + pagination. Also implement LicensePermissionGuard (ISS-016) to gate this page.

issues.title: useFreeQuotaUsage hook not migrated
issues.description: useFreeQuotaUsage hook exists in the original console and provides free tier quota data to the billing dashboard and usage widgets. It is not present in the migration's src/hooks/ directory. Components that depend on it either silently fail or show incorrect data for free-tier users.
issues.recommendation: Port useFreeQuotaUsage from the original. Identify all components that use it and verify they receive the data correctly after porting.

issues.title: useRtcAnnouncementTracking hook and rtc-announcement-tracking store not migrated
issues.description: useRtcAnnouncementTracking and its backing store rtc-announcement-tracking.ts are not present in the migration. These track which RTC product announcements a user has dismissed (stored in localStorage). Without them, dismissed announcements will re-appear on every page load.
issues.recommendation: Port useRtcAnnouncementTracking hook and create rtc-announcement-tracking.ts store with Jotai atom + localStorage persistence. The localStorage integration pattern should use the atomWithStorage utility from jotai/utils.
